levels.title: First watch
levels.tagline: Read the network. Trust the evidence. Make your throw.

briefing.text: Six incidents. Three possible diagnoses. Inspect both switches, compare the evidence, then aim at a diagnosis and throw your shuriken. Each incident has one supported problem category. No timer, lives, or penalty for retrying. After your diagnosis, read the field dispatch: receive CRC errors send the technician to the opposite optic; Remote Fault True sends them to that same side; Tx outside its alarm limits sends them to that transmitter. Flapping needs error or Remote Fault history to choose a side. These are this training runbook’s replacement recommendations; verify the link after the swap.

definitions.meaning: Inspect Rx power. For these ColorChip optics, −30 dBm means no light; values below −15.70 dBm are very bad light, not necessarily absent. Also check Tx: outside −9.00 to +3.30 dBm alarm limits supports a transmit-light problem.
Compare the same receiving interface at two times. A positive CRC delta with up states is evidence of new errors. Old totals alone are not.
Count actual up/down changes. Four or more inside the inclusive 60-second window qualifies in this game; it is a teaching threshold, not a universal EOS definition.

briefing.workedExample: A receiver has 30 CRC errors, then 38 a minute later. Normal light and a stable up history rule out the other two categories. The evidence supports 8 new CRC errors. It does not identify a failed component.

briefing.text: Six incidents. Three possible diagnoses. Inspect both switches, compare the evidence, then aim at a diagnosis and throw your shuriken. Each incident has one supported problem category. No timer, lives, or penalty for retrying. After your diagnosis, read the field dispatch: receive CRC errors send the technician to the opposite optic; Remote Fault True sends them to that same side; Tx outside its alarm limits sends them to that transmitter. Flapping needs error or Remote Fault history to choose a side. These are this training runbook’s replacement recommendations; verify the link after the swap.

definitions.meaning: Inspect Rx power. For these ColorChip optics, −30 dBm means no light; values below −15.70 dBm are very bad light, not necessarily absent. Also check Tx: outside −9.00 to +3.30 dBm alarm limits supports a transmit-light problem.
Compare the same receiving interface at two times. A positive CRC delta with up states is evidence of new errors. Old totals alone are not.
Count actual up/down changes. Four or more inside the inclusive 60-second window qualifies in this game; it is a teaching threshold, not a universal EOS definition.
